dialogue.Introduction: Ah, a new face. I am the Tax Collector, which means you will like me about as much as you like winter.#$b#But I am also the one keeping this town from falling apart, so you had better get used to me.$h
dialogue.Mon: Another Monday, another stack of receipts. Every week the ledger gets longer and nobody pays me any faster.
dialogue.Tue: Did you know the farm produce has been undertaxed for three seasons? I am not accusing anyone. I am just looking at you.
dialogue.Wed: Wednesday. Half the town owes me money and the other half owes money to the first half. It is a very tangled web.
dialogue.Thu: Thursday is for invoices. Friday is for audits. Please do not be on my list for either.
dialogue.Fri: Friday. The one day I can pretend my desk is tidy before the weekend mess arrives.
dialogue.Sat: Saturday, and the town square is busy with everyone selling something. Everyone except me. I am the one who takes the cut.
dialogue.Sun: Sunday. I am supposed to be resting, but my conscience keeps counting the week's sums. Ugh.
dialogue.Mon2: Two hearts already? You must be a good customer. Or a very sneaky one. I will decide which later.
dialogue.Thu2: I hear you have been fishing at the beach. Fish are not taxable, I checked. A pity, I would have loved to tax a fish.
dialogue.Tue6: Between us, the Tavernkeep owes me for three months. I do not dare collect it, the man is terrifying with a mop.
dialogue.Wed2: Did you know the mines are fully taxable? Every ore you carry out is a little piece of the town's future. Mostly mine.
dialogue.Wed6: Some days I wish I had taken up farming. Nobody sends a farmer a bill for the weather.
dialogue.Sat6: I used to dream of a quiet job in a small town. Turns out a small town means a very small pile of money to count.
dialogue.Fri10: You have become a regular part of my week, @. I suppose that means you are now on my books. Congratulations.
dialogue.Sun10: You have become rather important to me, @. Do not let it go to your head. I will only count it once.
dialogue.Mon10: A Monday with you feels lighter than it ought to. I think the ledger is missing a column, and the column is you.
dialogue.Mon4: Ah, @! Good morning. I have already been up for two hours counting the coins twice. What can I do for you?$h
dialogue.Tue4: The Nurse says I am the most boring man in the valley. She is not wrong, but she still stops by my desk anyway.$h
dialogue.Wed4: Wednesday mornings I like to walk the town square. It is the only time the mayor's manor feels like a home instead of an office.$h
dialogue.Thu4: The Angler wants to tax me for fishing rights. Bratty little so-and-so. You are much nicer company, @.$h
dialogue.Fri4: Fridays I review the disasters of the week. You have made a few of them less disastrous. Thank you for that.$h
dialogue.Sat4: A fine Saturday, @. The soup at the Luau is an excellent investment. I will be tallying the contributions, but I am glad you came.$h
dialogue.Sun4: Sundays are when I finally put my feet up. I would like you to join me sometime, if you bring a decent lemonade.$h
dialogue.Mon8: I will admit it, @. The paperwork is only half the reason I come out to talk to you. The other half is that I like having someone to talk to.$h
dialogue.Tue8: When my sister moved away the house got very quiet. Now the valley is full of people, and I think it suits an old tax man.$s
dialogue.Wed8: You know what I want more than gold? A quiet beach, a chair, and a fishing line that nobody bothers to audit.$h
dialogue.Thu8: I trust you more than the ledger, and I do not say that about anything with column headers.$h
dialogue.Fri8: I worry about the valley when the bosses come. Every monster is a bill for repairs. But I worry less when you are around.$s
dialogue.Sat8: If the goblins ever march again, I want you on my side. Even I cannot tax a goblin army into leaving.$u
dialogue.Sun8: Today I counted my savings and realized I could retire. But I would like to keep working, if only to keep an eye on you.$h
dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer Wednesday, and the sun makes my desk too warm. The ink runs and the numbers blur. I am not complaining, only sweating.$s
dialogue.summer_Sun: The summer sun is lovely, but the beach is crowded with tourists asking for directions to shops I do not own.$h
dialogue.summer_20: Midsummer days are long, and so are my lunch breaks. Strange, I have never taken a lunch break before this year.$h
dialogue.winter_Fri8: Winter Friday. Snow piles up on the manor steps and I am stuck inside with frosty ledgers. Come warm my desk, will you?$h
dialogue.winter_Tue2: Winter Tuesday. Please do not track snow onto my rug. Snow is taxable, you know.$u
dialogue.winter_25: Feast day. The town gives gifts this time, and I am told I am not allowed to tax the Feast. A miracle.$h
dialogue.fall_Mon: Fall Monday. The leaves keep landing in my ledger, and I swear they are filing a complaint against me.$h
dialogue.fall_15: The fifteenth of fall. Halfway through the harvest, halfway through my patience.$h
dialogue.spring_Sat4: Spring Saturday. The flowers are blooming and I am finally out of the office. I feel young again. Almost.$h
dialogue.spring_3: Early spring. The taxes are due and the town is in a panic, but at least the sun is out.$h

rainy: Rainy days are the only ones I do not mind staying indoors. The roof leaks in one corner, and I am charging myself rent for it.$h

situations.eye: The giant eye is gone from the skies. Good. It was staring at my ledger all night, and I am sure it was counting.$h
situations.evilBoss: The Eater of Worlds and the Brain of Cthulhu are both finished. The insurance claims from that mess will take a year to process.$s
situations.skeletron: Skeletron is defeated and the dungeon is open. The Old Man is free, and I suspect he will want a discount on his rent.$u
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is gone. The honey trade was a monopoly, and I have no idea what the prices will do now.$u
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh has fallen and hardmode has begun. The monsters got stronger, the prices got higher, and my tax rates are going up. Do not say I did not warn you.$a
situations.mechs: One of the mechanical bosses is destroyed. Clockwork machines are expensive to clean up, and I am sure the Mechanic will send me a bill.$h
situations.plantera: Plantera has been put to rest and the jungle temple is open. I have already drafted a tax on the jungle treasure. Do not ask me how.$h
situations.golem: The Golem has fallen. The temple's gold rubble must be surveyed and taxed, and I have never been so eager to do paperwork.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is defeated and the celestial pillars are open. A pillar tax would be an enormous number. I am already drafting the letters.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is gone and the sky is quiet again. A night without a cosmic horror means I might finally get some sleep.$h
situations.goblins: The goblin army was repelled last night. I counted them, and they still owe the town a fine for the broken fence.$a
situations.pirates: The pirates are gone. They tried to take my coins, but I suspect the Pirate will be sending his invoice to the sea.$h
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion is repelled and the snow is clearing. My feet are cold, but the books are, thankfully, dry.$h
situations.martians: The Martian Madness is over and the saucers have left our fields. I have billed the damage to the Martian Tax Office.$h
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night. The monsters came out, the town locked its doors, and I counted the coins under my mattress three times.$u
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark in a solar eclipse last night. I did not collect a single payment all day. Even the sky is behind on its taxes.$h
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today. I have been invited, which I find suspicious. I will go, but only to audit the snacks.$h

festivals.spring13: The Egg Festival! Everyone hides eggs and I hide my wallet. Nobody has ever found it, so I count that as a win.$h
festivals.spring24: The Flower Dance. I have not danced since the old days and I do not intend to start. But I will watch you, @, and count your steps.$h
festivals.summer11: The Luau. Everyone adds to the community soup and I stand there with a ledger and a tally. I put in a coin, and the soup is wonderful.$h
festivals.summer28: The Dance of the Moonlight Jellies. The jellies swim under the stars and the beach looks like a dream. A fine place to forget about numbers. For an hour.$h
festivals.fall16: The Stardew Valley Fair. Every stall pays a fee to me, and every prize ribbon is a little tax on the glory. I have never been happier to collect.$h
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve. They say the ghosts in the maze do not pay taxes. Those are the worst kind of residents.$u
festivals.winter8: The Festival of Ice. Ice fishing, snow sculptures, and a contest I have to judge fairly. Which means no bribes, @. I am watching you.$h
festivals.winter25: The Feast of the Winter Star. A secret gift exchange, and gifts are not taxed. Lovely. I have already picked something out for you.$h

loved.text: Gold! Real, honest gold. Now that is a gift a tax man can respect. Thank you, @.$h

liked.text: Gems, nice and shiny. Shiny things make my ledger look almost cheerful.$h

neutral.text: Dandelions. Not taxable and not valuable. I will take them anyway. Thank you, I suppose.

disliked.text: Ugh. Trash? I am a tax collector, not a rubbish bin.$a

hated.text: A boss summon? You want me to tax a monster sized disaster? Take it away this instant. Every boss costs this town a fortune.$a

events.after: Don't tell anyone I nearly cried over my ledger. It was only dust.

steps.say: Oh! @, you startled me. Never sneak up on a man with an open ledger.$u
Three hundred gold for the fence repair and not one coin paid. Nobody in this valley pays on time.$s
Not that I am complaining. Complaining is the one thing I do without a receipt.#$b#Now then, what can I do for you?$h

steps.question: Do you think I am too strict?

answers.reply: A little? Hmph. Perhaps a very small little.$h

answers.text: Not at all. A town needs its books in order.
answers.reply: Finally, someone with sense. Sit down, you are making the desk look untidy.$h

answers.text: I would pay double to never see you again.
answers.reply: Double? Now there is a figure I can work with.$a

steps.say: Well. You have made me lose my count. Forty-one, forty-two... no matter, I will start again tomorrow.$s
Oh, and @, the Merchant still owes me for a chair. Don't tell him I said so.$h

events.after: Five gold was a generous refund. Do not get used to it.

steps.say: @! Walk with me, I am doing my rounds. Every paving stone in this square gets a proper inspection.$h
I came here with one suitcase and a debt I had not earned. The square had weeds, nobody paid for anything, and the fountain was just a puddle.$s
Look at it now. Everyone pays for something, and the fountain is a proper fountain. I had a hand in that, you know.$h

steps.question: Are you happy with the taxes here?

answers.reply: Suppose? Ha! That is as close to a compliment as I give out.$h
Robbery! Well. Robbery with a receipt, at least.$a

steps.say: Between us, a man has to be paid to keep the lights on.#$b#And one day I would like a cottage by the beach. Waves, a chair, and no ledgers at all.$s
Don't tell anyone I want to retire. They would tax the idea.$h
Here, @. A tax refund. Five gold coins, the first I have ever handed out. Do not make a habit of asking.$h

events.after: Keep this between us. The Tavernkeep thinks I am a very stingy man, and I like it that way.

steps.say: Ah, @. Sit down. The Tavernkeep is pouring, and no, I am not paying for your drink.$h
Back in the old days I taxed the things that crawled out of the dungeon. Eye things, slime things, things with far too many legs.$u
They paid in teeth, mostly. Teeth. I could not balance a ledger with teeth.$s

steps.question: Why stay here instead of running off?

answers.text: Because the town needs a good accountant.
answers.reply: Exactly. Who else would keep this valley's figures from ruin?$h
Like? I suppose I do. Don't tell anyone, it is bad for my reputation.$h

answers.text: Because nobody else would hire you.
answers.reply: Ouch. Well, that is also true. Drink up and forget I said anything.$s

steps.say: The valley is the only place my ledgers ever balanced, @. I would not trade that for a mountain of gold.#$b#Please don't repeat that either.$h
Now the Tavernkeep says this round is on me. Oh, cheap, cheap. He can count the glasses himself.$h

events.after: Did I really tell you about my sister? Well. Best not mention it at the next audit.

steps.say: The tide is coming in and the moon is out, and here I stand. On a beach. At night. Don't you dare say a word.$u
My sister moved to the big city twenty years ago. We write letters, the only post I do not mind paying postage on.$s
Some days I think the valley needs me to keep it running. Other days I think I need it more. That is a terrible admission from a tax man.$h

steps.question: Do you miss your family too?

answers.reply: Then we both have good reason to keep writing letters.$s
Sometimes is enough, I think. It is the sort of thing that comes back around.$h
Hm. Good for you, then. Somebody has to keep the books.$a

steps.say: Thank you for listening, @. You are the only one in town who never asks about my audit.$h

events.after: Your fence is repaired, by the way. Do not tell the Merchant who paid for it.

steps.say: @! Don't look so surprised. The mayor visits his farm once a season, and this is my season.$h
Your parsnips are in very orderly rows. Better kept than my ledger, I will admit.$h
Now, about the old fence on this farm. Forty gold in fines. Paid, @. In full.$u
Don't look at me like that. The town books call it miscellaneous kindness. I invented that column just now.#$b#It is my only soft spot, and somehow it is in your field.$l

steps.question: Why did you pay it for me?

answers.reply: Mayor is a title. Friend is a better word, though I would rather not say it too loudly.$h

answers.text: That was very generous of you.
answers.reply: Shh! Generous is a word that will ruin my reputation.$h

steps.say: Here is a small token from the mayor's own desk. Keep it safe, it is worth more than it looks.$h
And don't tell the Merchant. He would want a cut of my kindness.$h
